summary: Tested the forgot-password flow end to end. BACKEND: new test_iter24_forgot_password.py, 5/5 passed. (1) A request for an existing user, by email in uppercase or by handle, returns 202 {status:accepted} and creates a reset token row. The email send through the Emergent email API raised no 'Email send refused' warning, sent to delivered+fp<tag>@resend.dev. (2) An unknown identifier returns the same 202 body, and a missing identifier returns 400/422. (3) The 3 per hour per user limit works: later requests still return 202 but create no token. (4) Confirm: a password under 10 chars returns 400 with a field error and does not use up the token; bogus and expired tokens return 400 TOKEN_INVALID. (5) A valid token returns 204, the old session's /auth/me goes to 401, the old password gets 401, the new password logs in with 200, and reusing the token returns 400. UI (1920x1080): Login 'Forgot Password?' link opens /forgot-password; submitting an email shows 'Check your inbox' with no dev-token box; 'Send another link' goes back to the form with the value kept. /reset-password?token=bogus shows 'This link is invalid or has expired.'; a short password shows a field error; a valid token (seeded straight into the DB because the real email can't be read) shows 'Password updated' then redirects to /login; the new password works and the old one fails. /reset-password without a token shows a 'Reset token' paste field. All TEST_ users were deleted afterwards. mailtest/demo were not touched.

minor.issue: A successful reset does not cancel the user's other unused reset tokens. After resetting, the other unused reset tokens (3 in the API test, 1 in the UI test) could still be used for up to 1 hour, so an older emailed link can change the password again.
An empty or whitespace identifier is accepted with 202. There is no length or empty check on IdentifierIn.

Timing leak: the email is sent inside the request (httpx with a 30s timeout), so an existing account takes about 0.5s and an unknown one about 0.15s. That lets someone tell which accounts exist. Send it as a background task (BackgroundTasks or asyncio.create_task).
The rate limiter (digest.allow_send_now) is per user and in memory. It resets on restart and isn't shared across workers, and there is no per-IP limit, so one IP can trigger emails for many accounts.

ui_bugs.issue: Submitting an empty field shows 'Check your inbox' (noValidate form + backend accepts ''). It should block empty submits on the client.

issues: With an invalid or expired token, the only error is 'This link is invalid or has expired.' There is no link to /forgot-password to get a new link, and the user can keep resubmitting.
No data-testid attributes on the inputs or buttons. Tests had to use #identifier, #password and button text.

action_items: In reset_confirm, after consume_token, mark all other unused reset tokens for that user as used: db.tokens.update_many({user_id, kind:'reset', used_at:None}, {$set:{used_at:now()}})
Check that identifier is not empty (strip, 1-254 chars) in reset_request and on the client
Move send_account_link out of the request path (background task) to remove the timing leak
Add a 'Request a new link' link to /forgot-password when confirm returns TOKEN_INVALID
Add data-testid to the forgot/reset password inputs and buttons
critical_code_review_comments: auth.py reset_request: an origin_of() of None (localhost or a host with a port) quietly skips the send, so nothing is logged if the email isn't sent. Add a warning log.

auth.py: hashing tokens with sha256, a single-use find_one_and_update and a 1h TTL are good. Validating the password before consume_token correctly keeps a weak-password attempt from using up the token.
reset_confirm revokes all sessions (good), but there is no 'password changed' notification email to the account owner.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of core flow; 1 low-priority validation bug

seed_data_creation: Temporary TEST users test_fp_<tag> / test_fpui_<tag> with delivered+...@resend.dev emails, all deleted. Reset tokens for the UI test were inserted straight into db.tokens (sha256 hash).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run pytest tests/test_iter24_forgot_password.py. It creates and cleans up its own user and inserts known reset tokens via motor, using MONGO_URL from backend/.env loaded with dotenv and never printed. The in-memory reset limit is 3 per hour per user, so a rerun within an hour on the same user would fail, but each run uses a new user. Don't use mailtest for repeated reset requests.
test_credentials: Used /app/memory/test_credentials.md as context. demo and mailtest were not modified.
